# Decisions: rust-core

- 2026-09-15T15:56:18.112Z — rule: **Hot-path event and projection behaviour is defined by docs/SPEC.md plus the conformance suite and must pass against both the TypeScript and Rust implementations; Rust schema types are generated from packages/schema/src, never hand-written.** — chose **Adopt Rust for sofar's HOT PATH, incrementally, starting now. Ruled by the run owner 2026-09-15 ("yes do it").
SUPERSEDES, for the hot path only, the CLAUDE.md engineering conventions:
- "TypeScript strict mode; Node ≥18; ES modules";
- "Dependencies: … Nothing else without logging a Decision". Rust crates are limited to serde, serde_json and ulid until another Decision adds one.

Scope of `sofar-core`: hook handlers (session-start, user-prompt-submit, post-tool-use, stop, session-end), atomic event append, fold, digest/status render, and statusline.

TypeScript keeps: the MCP server, `sofar drive`, init/doctor/review, and cloud commands.

The contract comes first: docs/SPEC.md plus a black-box conformance suite over commands, hook stdin/stdout, env and record bytes. It runs against BOTH implementations.

The schema rail holds: event payload types stay authored ONLY in packages/schema/src. Rust types are GENERATED from them, never hand-written. Projection templates keep one source of truth, and Rust output is verified byte-identical by golden tests.

Parity gate: 100% conformance, perf targets met, and a benchmark arm "sofar-rust-core" vs "sofar-ts" that shrinks no D19 lead margin.

Sequencing: r1-fixes waves 1–2 land in TypeScript now, and the Rust core must reach parity INCLUDING them. After parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only, which stops the TypeScript port surface growing. Distribution: prebuilt per-platform binaries through npm optionalDependencies, with a TypeScript fallback.** over 
- A big-bang rewrite now: it freezes waves 1–3, leaves round 2 unable to attribute gains, and means porting 27.6k engine lines and 34k test lines before anything is trustworthy.
- Staying TypeScript-only behind a measure-first gate: the run owner's point is that the port cost grows with every feature, and Codex CLI, Turborepo and Biome show the path is proven. because 
- Sofar runs on every tool call of every agent session. A native core gives near-zero hook start-up, fast folds over very large records (this repo's own is 9.7 MB), a single binary with no Node dependency for Codex/Cursor/OpenCode users, and headroom for many parallel agents.
- Measured 0.31 hooks are only ~0.75% of session time today, so the win is future scale and distribution rather than today's tokens. That is why it goes incrementally, and must pass the same benchmark gate as any other change.
- A conformance-first strangler port means neither implementation can drift from the SPEC.
- 2026-09-15T16:11:33.105Z — rule: **Hot-path Rust code reproduces the JavaScript text semantics pinned in docs/HOTPATH.md §Text-semantics pins, never Rust defaults; a parity difference is fixed in Rust or ruled by a Decision, never absorbed by loosening the conformance suite.** — chose **Byte parity is defined against the TypeScript engine's JavaScript text semantics, inventoried in docs/HOTPATH.md §Text-semantics pins: lengths and clips in UTF-16 code units, JS non-unicode regex classes, JS whitespace class, ECMAScript number formatting in canonical JSON, Node path.relative/basename, Math.round half-up, millisecond ISO timestamps. docs/HOTPATH.md is the hand-written contract inventory the conformance suite (1.2) drives; SPEC gaps it lists (G1–G15) are resolved by SPEC edits or Decisions, never by letting the two implementations differ.** over Rust-native defaults (char/byte lengths, Unicode-aware regex classes, ryu number formatting) with SPEC amended to tolerate the drift between implementations. because The 10k injection cap, every clip budget, the redaction and guard regexes and the canonical event bytes all decide observable output; a Rust core that used its own defaults would pass no golden test against the live 9.4 MB record and would fork events.jsonl bytes on identical events (the spurious-diff hazard SPEC §Event envelope exists to prevent). Reproducing JS semantics is cheap and mechanical; tolerating drift would make "same bytes from both implementations" (D1) unprovable.

Any improvement, idiom or best practice found that is not applied immediately is captured in this record as a note (sofar_add_note) or repo memory (sofar_remember), not left in a session's context. Byte parity (D1, D2) still bounds every change: an improvement may change how the bytes are produced, never which bytes.
- 2026-09-15T16:46:47.721Z — chose **The conformance suite (1.2) masks volatile bytes BY SHAPE instead of injecting a clock: a run-minted ulid becomes <ULID> only when its time part falls in the run's window, a run-minted ISO timestamp becomes <TS>, the two relative-age labels (Nm/Nh/Nd ago, ~Nh/~Nd since) become <AGO>, scratch paths become <ROOT>/<HOME>. Fixture bytes are never masked. Goldens are recorded from the TypeScript reference only, and only after the fixture horizon (newest fixture event + the 1 h cold-resume gap) so the presence of time-gated lines cannot flip. Everything else is pinned by building the child's environment from nothing but PATH (scratch HOME, git identity, XDG dirs, peer registry, update cache, LANG, TZ). Chosen under autonomy while the run owner's O6 ruling is outstanding; a SOFAR_NOW override can still be added later and would only shrink the mask list.** over Adding a test-only SOFAR_NOW clock override (plus a ulid seed) to the hot path so goldens compare unmasked, or leaving time-dependent surfaces out of the suite. because Masking needs no hot-path code change in either implementation, keeps the shape of every volatile field asserted (a malformed ulid or timestamp still fails), and ulid randomness would defeat an unseeded clock override anyway. Leaving session-start's time-gated lines out would drop the surface the 10k cap and preface composition depend on.
- 2026-09-15T18:33:19.261Z — rule: **A Rust perf claim is made only with `npm run perf` numbers (SOFAR_CONFORMANCE_BIN, same machine as a fresh reference run), never with in-process or hand-timed figures; the 3.3 gate is every cell's p50 and p95 at or under the recorded target.** — chose **The perf target for the Rust core is the checked-in TypeScript baseline (packages/engine/test/conformance/perf/baseline.typescript.json), recorded by the 1.3 runner with the same black-box method the conformance suite uses (one process per hook, spawn to exit, p50/p95 nearest rank over 20 spawns) across 10/100/1,000 initiatives × 1/10 MB bound logs, this repo's record and a no-record floor. The 3.3 gate (SOFAR_PERF_GATE=1) passes only when every candidate p50 AND p95 is ≤ the target in every cell, candidate and reference re-measured on the same machine in the same sitting.** over In-process micro-benchmarks of fold/render (would not count node boot, the part Rust removes, and cannot run against a binary); a single aggregate score (would let a 10 MB regression hide behind a 1 MB win); comparing against numbers recorded on another machine. because The user pays per spawn, so the measurement must include process start and be runnable against any implementation binary; per-cell p50 and p95 is the smallest set that catches both a median regression and a tail regression at each scale; hardware differences dwarf the margins being gated.

ADOPT WITH CONDITION: a sidecar `events.jsonl.lock` protocol both TypeScript and Rust implement (O_EXCL create + stale-lock recovery) plus an idempotency key in fold; a resolver shim rather than absolute binary paths in committed settings; a fold checkpoint validated by prefix hash + line count + last-line hash, any mismatch → full refold; schema codegen via ts-json-schema-generator pinned to TS 5.9/6 with a typify spike and a narrow emitter as fallback. This amends D1's runtime crate list to: serde, serde_json, ulid, lexopt. DEFER: WASM single core, tantivy, rmcp, rkyv, memmap2, mimalloc, PGO, WASI plugins, win32-arm64.
